name: Dragonfly
tagline: the hoverer: strafe, stop dead, dash
summary: The hoverer. The only hull whose velocity has nothing to do with its nose: the left stick thrusts in any direction (strafe, forward, back), the right stick looks, A and B climb and sink, LT stops it dead. RT is a dash: 190 u/s for a quarter second in the direction you are pushing, three pips that regrow, and nothing can touch you mid-dash. Twin-stick arena movement in 3D.

spec.v: left stick thrusts any way · RT dash (3 pips, i-frames) · LT brake
190 u/s × 0.25 s, a pip every 1.2 s
stamina dashes and strafes: Hades II, Silksong, ULTRAKILL, twin-stick arenas

fantasy: It does not fly, it hangs in the air and decides. Sidestep a trail, stare down a rival while sliding past, and dash through the gap nobody else fits.
why: The stamina-gated dash with invulnerability frames is 2025's most-shipped movement feature (Hades II at 95 Metacritic, Silksong 7M in three months, ULTRAKILL's three pips), and omnidirectional strafing is the arena-shooter control scheme the whole fleet lacks: every Cosmic Shore hull flies nose-first. The Dragonfly is the dodge-duel vessel.

notModelled: The game's dual-stick mix does not apply: the Dragonfly needs its own input strategy (left stick = translation, right stick = look), the first in the fleet.
A dash's i-frames ignore hull contacts here; what they mean against a Grizzly blast or a danger prism is a design question.
sources: Design: Docs/Studios/CONCEPT_FLEET.md (Dragonfly). The Scarab's juke dash and the Sparrow's turret stance are the nearest shipped relatives.
